newsitem.title: GERMANY: Pre-Easter caution hurts German shares.
newsitem.headline: Pre-Easter caution hurts German shares.

text.p: Pre-Easter caution weighed on the German share market on Thursday, sending the market sharply lower in late trade after enthusiasm for the car and financial sectors buoyed prices in the bourse session.
Pressured by weak Bunds and Wall Street, the IBIS DAX index ended the day down 31.39 points at 3,407.83, well off the DAX's closing level at mid-afternoon.

The DAX had risen 10.93 points, or 0.3 percent, to close the bourse session at 3,429.05 points, catching up with an advance in post-bourse trade on Wednesday after strong earnings data from giant Daimler-Benz.
Car shares were the stars, with the DAX 100 car sector index advancing six times faster than the market average, with a 1.8 percent overall gain.

BMW rose 45 marks to 1,350 marks, VW closed up 19.30 marks at 922 marks while Daimler, which returned to a 2.8 billion mark profit in 1996 after 1995's unprecedented loss and is to reinstate its dividend, rose 1.70 marks to 133.40 in bourse trade, before falling back to 132.50 marks in IBIS.
"Those numbers (Daimler's) were really well above what people expected. They had an even bigger impact because they weren't expected at all until next month," said a Frankfurt dealer.

The overall mood was uncertain ahead of the Easter holiday. On the one hand, dealers noted that institutional investors had been leading the buying move. But more bearish talk that this week's U.S. interest rate hike was not the last was also circulating.
Despite the long-anticipated U.S. rate hike, the DAX has risen four percent this week.
"The share market will see stronger volatility in the coming weeks," Commerzbank warned in a note to investors.

"More favourable prospects for the German economy and the resultant opportunities for more improvements in corporate earnings will be offset by possible pressure from the foreign exchange and interest rate side."

Bank shares were also relatively firm, with top takeover targets Bayerische Hypotheken- und Wechsel Bank and Bayerische Vereinsbank up 50 pfennigs at 58.30 marks and up 1.85 marks at 69.10 marks respectively in bourse trade.
Hypo-Bank ended IBIS trade at 57.95 marks and Vereinsbank ended at 69 marks.
Fresh talk of mergers in the banking sector, mainly driven by rumour, has fuelled renewed interest in financial shares.

"Everyone wants into banks again all at once," commented one trader. "Although we've seen this week what we can expect from hostile takeover attempts in Germany," he added, referring to the aborted takeover bid by Krupp for steel firm Thyssen.
Thyssen shares rose 1.50 marks to 376.50 marks in bourse trade and closed IBIS at 375.50, after it and Krupp finalised their co-operation, with a steel venture to be 60 percent controlled by Thyssen.

The news has generally been viewed as a negative for the German market, which had perked up at the chance of an Anglo-Saxon style takeover, but also revived talk of consolidation in the overcrowded banking industry.
